item.title: Why do we think we understand the world more than we actually do?
item.description:
📝 The illusion of explanatory depth (IOED) describes our belief that we understand more about the world than we actually do. That is, it’s only when we explain something that the gaps in our knowledge become apparent to us. The illusion of the explanatory gap is something that we’re subject to from an early age, with studies showing that children as young as kindergarten overestimate their explanatory knowledge.
🔗 Read more: https://thedecisionlab.com/biases/the-illusion-of-explanatory-depth

item.title: Residential Proxies Are a National Security Threat
item.description:
📝 Residential Proxies Are a National Security Threat Jul 22, 2026 US residential proxies are the bane of the internet. This is why bad actors love US residential proxies, their abuse comes from the same addresses as genuine users. ISPs should warn their customers At the very least, major American ISPs (Comcast, AT&T) should detect clearly suspicious activity coming from customer IPs and warn them to scan their computers, check their TV apps, and find whatever is turning their internet into a proxy.
🔗 Read more: https://jacob.gold/posts/residential-proxies-are-a-national-security-threat/

item.title: An Uncomplicated Man
item.description:
📝 Unlike some of Nolan’s other films, The Odyssey is not boring, thanks to the source material, which is impossible to mess up entirely. If only the human characters had been treated with such serious attention. Some seventh-century BCE Greek communities were ruled by an oligarchy, some by a single man.
🔗 Read more: https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v48/n14/emily-wilson/an-uncomplicated-man
